sources.author: Oliver Dietrich · Göbekli Tepe Research Project
sources.title: Of animals and a headless man: Pillar 43
sources.note: Excavation-team account. Separates visible motifs from alternative readings of the disc and arched forms.

sources.author: Göbekli Tepe Research Project
sources.title: Our project: site and research context
sources.note: Places the site in the tenth and ninth millennia BCE. Contextual site chronology is not a direct measurement of every carving.

sources.author: British Museum
sources.title: Hoa Hakananai’a · Oc1869,1005.1
sources.note: Object identity and carvings. Exact chronology of successive carving episodes remains uncertain; an object date must not date every later mark.

sources.author: British Museum
sources.title: Moai: history and Rapanui relationships
sources.note: Ancestral significance, removal from Orongo in 1868, and the living relationship with Rapanui communities. Direct page intermittently returns 403; indexed text checked in the source review.

sources.author: Mike Pitts, James Miles, Hembo Pagi & Graeme Earl
sources.title: Hoa Hakananai’a: a new study
sources.note: Digital recording and carving sequence. The proposed fledgling narrative is an interpretation, not the only reading.

sources.author: Mike Pitts
sources.title: Back stories: new insights into the Rapa Nui statues
sources.note: Researcher’s account of the 1917 geological sampling. The small plugged hole low on the right of the back is distinct from the large central ring.

sources.author: British Museum / Google Arts & Culture
sources.title: Birdman boulder · Oc1920,0506.1
sources.note: Orongo provenance, Routledge collection, dimensions and an egg interpretation; catalogue creation range 1750–1875 is approximate.

sources.author: Katherine Routledge
sources.title: The Mystery of Easter Island · figure 112; pp. 261–263
sources.note: Early photograph and reported accounts of the birdman competition. A colonial-period, mediated record; it does not exhaust Rapanui knowledge.

sources.author: Moreno-Mayar et al.
sources.title: Ancient Rapanui genomes reveal resilience and pre-European contact with the Americas
sources.note: Genetic evidence for Native American ancestry and contact before European arrival. Does not connect a particular motif to Anatolia. Open full text of the Nature paper, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07881-4.

sources.author: Museo Antropológico Padre Sebastián Englert
sources.title: Painted slabs from the ceremonial village of Orongo
sources.note: Local comparative material: painted birdman figures. A useful next reference set alongside the rock carvings.

sources.author: Graham Hancock
sources.title: Magicians of the Gods: author’s account
sources.note: Primary source for his proposed lost Ice Age civilisation and travelling survivors. A statement of a hypothesis, not independent corroboration.
